posts.name: srinath
posts.cooked:
What is the meaning of this statement?
cal will not be executed where date will exit with the status 0.

By this statement ‘ps && file *’ will be executed sequentially’,

does that mean these 2 commands can get executed sequentially soon after ls command also, not necessarily at the last?

posts.name: Santhana Krishnan S
posts.cooked:
ls; date || cal; ps && file *

The above is the concatenation of three independent commands in a single line. The equivalent woulb be

ls 
date || cal # || is logical OR. If date exits with *non-zero status* then only cal will be executed. 
ps && file * # && is logical AND. If ps exits with *zero status* then only file * will be executed.

posts.name: srinath
posts.cooked: In this problem, there’s no mention of zero status(success) or non-zero status(failure) for date. So, can’t we choose Option 2 also as it is the case that happens when date has non-zero status(failure) and cal gets executed?

posts.name: Santhana Krishnan S
posts.cooked:
By default date command is do not require arguments and is pre-installed in the Ubuntu. So if you execute the command date will not exit with a non-zero status.

If date exits with non-zero yes, cal will be executed. Still, option b is not correct because it did not include the date command.
